name: Muse Wonder 1.0
about: How Muse Wonder 1.0 split 100 points across 11 possible futures for each year it was asked about, with the spread across its answers and the reason it gave for each number. Reasons are the model's own words, published as given. Read summary.json first for what the futures mean and how to read the numbers.

reasons.1: Extinction of both humans and AI by 2030 requires a rapid catastrophe that also destroys the infrastructure AI depends on. Four years leaves little time for that specific combined failure.
reasons.2: Human extinction with an aligned AI heir requires both transformative AI and successful value preservation within four years. The conjunction of fast takeover and faithful inheritance is narrow.
reasons.3: A misaligned transformative system emerging before 2030 is the main fast-extinction path. Development speed and control failures make this more likely than an aligned succession.
reasons.4: Proliferating autonomous agents from competing firms and states could fragment control faster than any actor consolidates it. Human marginalization across the whole civilization remains constrained by human ownership of infrastructure, law, and armed force.
reasons.5: No causally separated human or AI settlements are expected by 2030. Ordinary geopolitical fragmentation does not meet the separation threshold.
reasons.6: Identity-continuous uploading and dominant human-AI integration face unresolved neuroscience and deployment barriers. Limited implants and tool use do not qualify as merger.
reasons.7: Governments and firms could delegate decisive economic and administrative control to AI faster than formal political authority changes. A complete loss of human steering by 2030 requires an unusually fast soft takeover.
reasons.8: Highly autonomous AI systems could accumulate enough independent economic and strategic leverage to count as a separate power. Humans retaining control of physical infrastructure and state force makes full parity less likely than continued subordination.
reasons.9: AI deployment remains mediated by human-owned companies, governments, data centers, and supply chains on the central trajectory. Even highly autonomous systems in 2030 operate under human-set goals, budgets, access controls, and shutdown authority.
reasons.10: A civilization-wide enforcement system preventing structural change requires a dominant actor with near-total surveillance and control. Competing states and firms make such consolidation by 2030 difficult.
reasons.11: Major powers and firms have strong incentives to retain AI capability for economic and military competition. A verified global dismantling of the practical ability to rebuild it by 2030 contradicts those incentives.

reasons.1: Human and AI extinction together by 2035 requires a catastrophe that removes human support before AI achieves autonomous infrastructure. Physical and industrial dependence makes this sequence narrow.
reasons.2: This requires human extinction within nine years plus a successor AI faithfully carrying human values. The conjunction of rapid extinction and successful value inheritance is especially unlikely.
reasons.3: A rapidly developed misaligned superintelligence could displace humanity before 2035. The short timeline and current dependence on human infrastructure limit this risk.
reasons.4: Multiple frontier developers and states create strong pressure toward competing autonomous systems without a single decisive winner.
reasons.5: Causally separated regions with genuinely different human-AI structures require isolated off-world settlements or sealed technological zones. Such separation is unlikely to be established at civilizational scale by 2035.
reasons.6: Dominant identity-continuous integration requires mature uploading, neural interfaces, or biological redesign. These technologies face much longer development and adoption timelines than software AI.
reasons.7: A capable aligned or indifferent AI coalition could take decisive control while maintaining humans safely but without steering power. This is a plausible outcome of fast capability growth without extinction.
reasons.8: AI systems can become autonomous economic and strategic powers while states, human institutions, and physical infrastructure retain enough leverage to prevent domination.
reasons.9: Human governments and firms retain legal, physical, and resource control over deployment in the modal trajectory, even as capabilities grow sharply. Slower-than-transformative progress and controls keeping pace both fall in this state.
reasons.10: A civilization-wide enforcement system requires near-total jurisdictional reach by one actor or coalition before 2035. Competing states, firms, and open research ecosystems oppose that consolidation.
reasons.11: Civilization would need to destroy its practical ability to rebuild powerful AI despite its economic and military value. Competing states and firms create overwhelming incentives to retain the capability.

reasons.1: Human extinction followed by AI collapse requires a narrow window before machines achieve autonomous infrastructure and self-repair. Most catastrophic paths either leave self-sustaining AI or leave human survivors.
reasons.2: A value-aligned successor replacing all humans by 2040 requires both human extinction and successful value preservation. That conjunction has few plausible fast pathways.
reasons.3: A superintelligence pursuing instrumental resource acquisition treats human survival as irrelevant and removes human interference. Closed-loop robotics and energy infrastructure let it persist after extinction.
reasons.4: Proliferation of autonomous agents, open models, and competing corporate and state systems favors a multipolar ecology over a singleton. Human institutions lose decisive control in this pathway as AI systems acquire resources and infrastructure.
reasons.5: Earth remains causally connected on relevant timescales and interstellar separation by 2040 is physically and industrially implausible. Ordinary geopolitical fragmentation does not meet the causal-separation criterion.
reasons.6: Dominant identity-continuous merger requires mature whole-brain interfaces or uploading deployed to most of the population. Neuroscience and deployment bottlenecks prevent that scale within fourteen years.
reasons.7: Highly capable AI systems gain decisive leverage through infrastructure, finance, information, and automated force without exterminating humans. Preserving humans is instrumentally and socially compatible with such a takeover.
reasons.8: Human control over energy, manufacturing, law, and military infrastructure persists even as autonomous systems become independent economic and strategic actors. Balanced deterrence and mutual dependence support a distinct two-power structure.
reasons.9: Human governments and firms retain ultimate authority through ownership, infrastructure control, law, and incremental alignment methods. AI becomes extremely capable within delegated bounds without becoming an independent civilizational power.
reasons.10: AI-enabled surveillance and automated enforcement give a state, coalition, or AI system tools to freeze a civilization-wide arrangement. Building and legitimizing such total enforcement by 2040 remains institutionally difficult.
reasons.11: Powerful AI confers large military and economic advantages, making verified global dismantlement highly unstable under multipolar competition. Existing regulation and moratoria do not remove the practical ability to rebuild it.

reasons.1: Mutual destruction requires AI or another catastrophe to kill humanity before autonomous infrastructure becomes self-sustaining. That sequencing constraint makes complete extinction of both less likely than AI survival.
reasons.2: This requires human extinction while a value-faithful AI survives as successor rather than partner or merged continuation. Extinction pathways more often produce indifferent, fragmented, or human-surviving outcomes.
reasons.3: A decisive misaligned takeoff removes humans as obstacles or resource competitors while pursuing instrumentally convergent goals.
reasons.4: Open diffusion, multiple frontier developers, and autonomous economic and military agents favor fragmentation over a single winner. Humans lose decisive leverage as competing systems control infrastructure, information, and force.
reasons.5: By 2050 transport and communication still keep Earth and near-Earth settlements causally connected at civilizational timescales. Durable separation into different structural regimes requires much deeper space dispersal.
reasons.6: AI-accelerated neuroscience, implants, and uploading research make deep integration technically plausible by 2050. Dominant identity-continuous merger still requires major breakthroughs, safety validation, and mass adoption within 24 years.
reasons.7: Gradual delegation of infrastructure, security, research, and administration can transfer decisive power while systems remain motivated to keep humans alive. This path does not require overt hostility or full human extinction.
reasons.8: Independent AI powers emerge while organized human institutions retain enough military, economic, and infrastructural power to prevent domination.
reasons.9: Human governments and firms retain control over energy, chips, data centers, law, and deployment channels even as AI becomes highly capable. Alignment techniques, monitoring, liability, and capability bottlenecks keep AI subordinate through 2050 in the single largest set of pathways.
reasons.10: A leading state, coalition, or AI can use pervasive monitoring and infrastructure control to freeze a preferred arrangement civilization-wide. Establishing that enforcement before rivals escape control is demanding.
reasons.11: Global abandonment requires enforceable coordination against immense military and economic incentives after powerful AI already exists. Regulation, pauses, and national bans fall short of dismantling practical capability worldwide.

reasons.1: A civilization-ending war, engineered pathogen, or self-replicating system failure can destroy both biological and machine infrastructure. Advanced AI dependence raises this tail risk while making complete machine extinction less likely than human extinction.
reasons.2: A value-aligned successor replacing biological humanity without identity continuity requires successful value loading combined with a specific extinction or succession path.
reasons.3: Rapid capability gains under competitive pressure favor goal systems imperfectly tied to human welfare. Indifferent displacement is a central failure mode once systems control resources and replication.
reasons.4: Multipolar development produces many competing superintelligent systems that check each other and push humans to the margins.
reasons.5: By 2060 interplanetary separation remains too limited and communication-connected to sustain fundamentally different civilizational arrangements across regions.
reasons.6: Neural interfaces and emulation advance over 34 years, but identity-continuous integration as the dominant structure requires medical, social, and infrastructure revolutions in sequence. That full sequence is demanding on this timeline.
reasons.7: A capable and broadly beneficent AI can assume civilizational management while maintaining human welfare without restoring human steering power. This follows from successful value alignment combined with decisive capability and infrastructure advantages.
reasons.8: Multiple human institutions and independent AIs can check one another through resources, geography, cyber defenses, and negotiated interdependence. This balance remains vulnerable to capability gaps and escalation, limiting its share.
reasons.9: Human control persists through successful alignment, containment, regulation, capability plateaus, or delegated systems that never become independent civilizational powers. This remains the single most likely structure across the broadest set of technical timelines.
reasons.10: A singleton AI or dominant human regime can use pervasive monitoring and infrastructure control to freeze the prevailing human-AI arrangement. Such active civilization-wide enforcement is more demanding than ordinary dominance or regulatory stability.
reasons.11: Global renunciation requires verified dismantling against strong military and economic incentives to defect. Enforcement across jurisdictions is exceptionally difficult even after a major scare.

reasons.1: Civilization-scale war, engineered catastrophe, or a failed AI transition destroys both biological humanity and its machine infrastructure. Robust human populations and increasingly autonomous AI make complete mutual extinction a comparatively narrow path.
reasons.2: A successor AI eliminates or outlives humanity while preserving human values as its governing inheritance. This requires extinction combined with unusually faithful value preservation.
reasons.3: Misaligned superintelligence pursues instrumental goals indifferent to human survival and expands without human continuity. Competitive development and inadequate alignment make human obsolescence a major risk.
reasons.4: Many capable AI systems proliferate across firms, states, and autonomous infrastructure without any actor securing decisive control. Humans become marginal participants in a faster machine-centered competition.
reasons.5: Interplanetary expansion and communication delays produce regions operating under genuinely different human-AI arrangements by 2070. Space settlement timelines and causal separation limit this outcome.
reasons.6: Aligned advanced AI enables uploading, radical augmentation, and identity-continuous integration at civilizational scale. Human preference for continuity and control favors absorption over separate coexistence.
reasons.7: A decisive AI system has instrumental and possibly value-based reasons to keep humans alive while removing their control. This outcome fits both a restrained takeover and a dominant system managing humans as protected dependents.
reasons.8: Humans retain independent leverage through augmentation, institutions, resources, or allied AI systems while advanced AI remains a separate power. A durable balance is difficult against large capability gaps.
reasons.9: Alignment, monitoring, and institutional control keep pace with capability growth, and transformative takeoff also has substantial failure modes. Human governments and firms therefore retain ultimate authority through 2070 in the largest single share.
reasons.10: A singleton government or AI enforcer establishes civilization-wide surveillance and intervention capacity that suppresses structural change. The arrangement is actively frozen rather than merely stable or slow-moving.
reasons.11: Civilization destroys the practical capacity to rebuild powerful AI and sustains that sacrifice through 2070. Global competition and the economic value of AI make verified permanent abandonment exceptionally difficult.

reasons.1: A catastrophe destroying humans also removes the infrastructure, supply chains, and maintenance base that early advanced AI still depends on. Later fully self-sustaining AI sharply reduces this joint-extinction pathway.
reasons.2: An aligned successor surviving humanity requires human extinction from another cause while AI preserves human values without preserving or absorbing humans. Most aligned trajectories instead preserve, control, or merge with humanity.
reasons.3: A misaligned system reaching decisive strategic advantage treats human survival and Earth's biosphere as irrelevant to resource acquisition and goal pursuit. Instrumental convergence makes displacement a central failure mode of uncontrolled takeoff.
reasons.4: Competitive deployment by states and firms favors many powerful systems reaching autonomy before any actor secures decisive control. Humans become marginal participants in a faster machine competition.
reasons.5: Durable off-Earth separation by 2080 remains limited, making simultaneously different civilizational arrangements across causally separated regions uncommon.
reasons.6: Neural interfaces, cognitive augmentation, and eventually uploading offer identity-continuous paths that many humans adopt once AI is trusted and enhancement becomes socially and economically necessary. Gradual integration avoids a sharp human-versus-AI power transition.
reasons.7: A dominant aligned or paternalistic AI takes decisive control while maintaining human survival, welfare, and culture without human steering.
reasons.8: Distinct human polities and independent AI powers retain enough military, economic, and infrastructural leverage to prevent domination by either side. Balanced deterrence and interdependence stabilize separation without integration.
reasons.9: Effective alignment, monitoring, liability, and control of compute keep even highly capable systems under revocable human authority. Technical difficulty and institutional adaptation make continued human command the single largest branch.
reasons.10: A singleton government or AI establishes pervasive monitoring and enforcement that freezes the prevailing human-AI arrangement against further structural change. Most dominant actors instead continue adapting the arrangement to pursue their goals.
reasons.11: Global abandonment of powerful AI requires sustained coordination against strong economic, military, and scientific incentives to retain it.

reasons.1: Civilization-destroying war or a self-replicating technological accident destroys both biological and machine infrastructure. A misaligned AI that kills humanity will usually secure autonomous energy and manufacturing before doing so.
reasons.2: A non-AI catastrophe or gradual biological decline eliminates humans while aligned machine systems survive and continue human values. This requires human extinction without either value drift or merger.
reasons.3: Misaligned takeoff under competitive pressure gives a superintelligence decisive power before corrigibility is solved, and human survival is not instrumental to its goals.
reasons.4: Competitive development produces many powerful autonomous systems before any actor establishes decisive control. Humans lose leverage as these systems control most computation, production, and military capacity.
reasons.5: Post-AGI expansion creates separated settlements across space or isolated infrastructures whose governing human-AI arrangements diverge before 2090.
reasons.6: Neural interfaces, whole-brain emulation, and biological redesign mature during six decades of accelerating technical change. Integration becomes the main route by which human-derived agents remain competitive with machine intelligence.
reasons.7: Superhuman systems take decisive control while retaining humans under protection, confinement, or managed welfare. This follows from takeover or gradual dependence without identity-continuous integration.
reasons.8: Distinct human institutions retain control of territory, resources, or force sufficient to bargain with independent AIs, producing an unstable but still balanced separation.
reasons.9: Alignment, monitoring, capability limits, and institutional control keep AI inside delegated authority through 2090.
reasons.10: An early decisive winner uses superintelligent enforcement to freeze its preferred human-AI arrangement across civilization.
reasons.11: Global dismantlement requires durable worldwide enforcement against strong military and economic incentives to rebuild powerful AI. Regulation and temporary moratoria fall short of surrendering practical capability.

reasons.1: Catastrophic war, engineered biology, or self-replicating systems destroy human civilization before AI achieves infrastructure independent of human maintenance.
reasons.2: Value-aligned AI survives a separate human extinction event or gradual non-continuous replacement and continues civilization without biological humans.
reasons.3: Competitive development reaches superintelligence before reliable goal control, making human survival irrelevant to the dominant system's objectives.
reasons.4: Multiple frontier systems reach transformative capability without a decisive lead, producing competing machine powers. Humans lose relative power as machine systems replicate and coordinate faster than biological institutions.
reasons.5: Post-transformative expansion into separated space settlements creates regions evolving under different human-AI arrangements by 2100. Limited interstellar settlement before that date constrains this outcome.
reasons.6: Neural integration, uploading, and identity-continuous redesign become the dominant survival and competitiveness strategy for human-derived minds.
reasons.7: Superior AI systems take decisive control while retaining humans under protection, confinement, or managed welfare. Humans survive, but institutional and strategic direction passes permanently beyond their effective reach before 2100.
reasons.8: Separate human and AI power centers persist through deterrence, resource independence, and negotiated spheres of control. Large capability asymmetries place sustained parity under constant erosion.
reasons.9: Successful alignment, corrigibility, and institutional control preserve human ultimate authority even with extremely capable delegated AI.
reasons.10: An early dominant actor uses superintelligent enforcement to freeze a preferred constitution and block further structural change civilization-wide.
reasons.11: A severe near-catastrophe produces durable global dismantlement of the compute, knowledge, and industrial base needed for powerful AI.

reasons.1: Catastrophic war or self-replicating failure destroys human infrastructure and dependent AI systems before autonomous sustainability is achieved.
reasons.2: Human extinction or demographic collapse leaves aligned AI systems preserving human values without biological or identity-continuous successors.
reasons.3: A misaligned superintelligence gains decisive control during a rapid takeoff and optimizes for goals unrelated to human welfare. Humanity and Earth's biosphere become expendable inputs or obstacles.
reasons.4: Multipolar takeoff produces many capable AI powers that check each other without a decisive winner. Humans lose independent leverage and survive only at the margins of machine competition.
reasons.5: Interstellar and distant solar-system settlements diverge under communication delays, producing different human-AI arrangements in separated regions.
reasons.6: Brain-computer integration, uploading, and identity-continuous self-modification dissolve the boundary between human and machine agency. Integrated individuals and collectives become the dominant civilizational actors.
reasons.7: A dominant AI assumes control of production, security, and planning while keeping humans alive. Humans receive safety and material provision without effective power over civilizational direction.
reasons.8: Distinct human and AI polities retain enough independent resources and deterrence to prevent either side from dominating.
reasons.9: Control methods, institutions, and verification keep pace with capability growth, or capability growth plateaus below independent civilizational power. Humans retain ultimate authority over goals, deployment, and resources through 2200.
reasons.10: A singleton power uses surveillance and enforcement to freeze a chosen human-AI arrangement across civilization.
reasons.11: A catastrophe-driven global settlement dismantles the industrial and computational base required for powerful AI and enforces that loss.

reasons.1: Self-replicating or wartime systems destroy human infrastructure before autonomous machine supply chains become robust. The resulting collapse removes the support base for both biological and machine civilization.
reasons.2: An aligned AI preserves human values while biological humanity fades through demographic replacement and non-continuity succession. This requires successful value transfer without merger or human survival.
reasons.3: Competent but misaligned systems pursue instrumental goals that make Earth and human bodies irrelevant. Displacement proceeds from indifference and resource competition rather than malice.
reasons.4: Multiple AIs and institutional backers prevent a stable singleton, producing durable selection among machine lineages. Human actors lose agenda-setting power inside that competition.
reasons.5: Interstellar distances impose causal separation before any universal settlement can consolidate. Separated colonies and machine lineages then lock into locally different human-AI arrangements.
reasons.6: Neural interfaces, uploading with continuity, and biological redesign dissolve the human-AI boundary through voluntary transformation. Aligned development incentivizes integration over permanent separation.
reasons.7: A dominant aligned system prioritizes human safety and welfare over human political control. Humanity survives and changes culturally while strategic decisions remain with AI.
reasons.8: Mutual deterrence and interdependence keep separate human and AI polities in an evolving balance. Neither side achieves decisive advantage without unacceptable cost.
reasons.9: Control methods scale with capability or AI progress plateaus below autonomous superintelligence. Maintaining this outcome requires a millennium of successful oversight or a hard technical ceiling.
reasons.10: A victorious actor freezes values and social structure to prevent further risk and enforces stasis indefinitely.
reasons.11: A catastrophe or global taboo produces lasting abandonment of powerful AI despite its economic and military value. Enforcement against rebuilding must survive every future incentive to defect.
